items.title: Autom8Labs launches AEC skills for AI agents
items.excerpt: Autom8Labs released MCP-based skills that guide AI agents through tasks in Revit, AutoCAD, 3ds Max, Grasshopper and other design tools.
items.rationale: New product release: MCP skills that let agents work inside Revit, AutoCAD, 3ds Max and Grasshopper. Architects can use it right away.

items.title: From a Figma frame to an AEM EDS block in one command
items.excerpt: Open-source kit: paste a Figma frame link and get an Adobe Experience Manager Edge Delivery block (JS, CSS, Universal Editor model) via REST or the Figma MCP server, within Figma's rate limits.
items.rationale: New open-source kit that turns a Figma frame into a working AEM Edge Delivery block over Figma MCP. It is a concrete handoff tool for enterprise sites.

items.title: Vercel MCP now renders deployments as an interactive card
items.excerpt: Vercel MCP now renders interactive deployment cards inside MCP Apps clients like ChatGPT, so status, build logs and debugging happen as generative UI in the chat.
items.rationale: Primary-source changelog showing MCP Apps generative UI in production, a working pattern for designers who build in-chat interfaces.

items.title: Code-based prototyping: When it's worth the setup
items.excerpt: Eleken's head of design explains why the agency now prototypes with real components, including Claude-generated interactive dashboards, to test states and edge cases that static Figma mockups hide.
items.rationale: A design agency's practical account of when to prototype in code with Claude-generated components instead of static Figma mockups. Teams can apply it on their next project.

items.title: Is this the most controversial font since Comic Sans?
items.excerpt: Creative Bloq on the aggressive, slanted brush-script typeface that has become the giveaway of AI-generated posters in cafes and village halls, and why small businesses keep using it.
items.rationale: Typography angle: one brush-script face has become the tell of AI-generated posters, which shows how AI defaults shape everyday visual culture.
